nodes.label: Repository Abstraction Swap
nodes.rationale: Switching deps.py from SimulatedServoRepository to BridgeServoRepository changes nothing above that line: services, API, GUI and every test stay as they are. That swap is the whole point of the abstraction.

nodes.label: run_dev.py Dev-PC Entrypoint
nodes.rationale: Exists because two imports only live on the board (arduino.app_utils and possibly Logger461). It points DB_PATH and LOG_FILE at local files, then boots the app the way main.py does minus the Bridge relay.

nodes.label: .env.board Copy Is The Only Manual Step
nodes.rationale: Forgetting it is silent: without .env, use_hardware_servo defaults to false, the backend runs the simulator, and the UI moves convincingly while the real servo never twitches. It is not shipped as .env because a dev machine would then drive hardware during pytest.
nodes.norm_label: .env.board copy is the only manual step

nodes.label: Wipe Before adb push
nodes.rationale: adb push overwrites files it copies but does not delete anything already on the board that is missing from the source, so renamed or deleted files linger and can be picked up instead of the new ones.

nodes.label: Bench-Measured Settings
nodes.rationale: Every configured value came from the diagnostic app on real hardware, not a datasheet.

nodes.label: No Modulus-360 Wrapping
nodes.rationale: In a multi-turn system -25 and 335 degrees are different absolute targets a whole output revolution apart, and wrapping would hide turn-count errors.

nodes.label: timestamp Never ts
nodes.rationale: Renamed everywhere: entities, schemas, DB columns, CSV first column, query params and tests. Descriptive naming over abbreviation.

nodes.label: angle_fault Status Flag
nodes.rationale: Sixth fault flag from status register bit 4, added end-to-end: entity, schema, /state, DB plus migration, CSV contract and GUI tile.

nodes.label: Multi-Turn Support
nodes.rationale: Not needed at plus/minus 90 degrees but kept because it is bench-proven: configure_range() applies angle limits 0, angle-resolution amplification and phase BIT4. Widening travel later is two numbers in .env, not a code change.

nodes.label: Pin The arduino:zephyr Core Version
nodes.rationale: Board Manager does not exist on the air-gapped machine, so the target must already have arduino:zephyr at the version built against (0.56.0 or newer, which adds Serial3 and the UNO Q main-thread-priority fix). Most likely cause of 'it worked on my laptop'.

nodes.label: check_bridge_contract.py
nodes.rationale: Every function crossing the MCU/Linux boundary is declared twice and nothing makes the compiler or interpreter compare them. A wrong argument count compiles and imports cleanly on both sides and fails at runtime as silence. Non-zero exit so it can go in a pre-commit hook.

nodes.label: Verify The Ethernet Patch Survived
nodes.rationale: ~/.arduino15/internal/ is a user-global cache shared by every app. Three or more matches for IPAddress((uint32_t) means the patch is intact; zero means App Lab re-fetched the library and it must be re-applied.

nodes.label: Confirm Which Backend Is Live
nodes.rationale: Two ways: the system health endpoint reports servo_backend, and the Python tab logs it at startup with a warning if simulated.

nodes.label: No Bricks Constraint
nodes.rationale: A brick pulls a Docker container from the internet the first time it is used, which cannot happen on the air-gapped target. The UI is served by FastAPI itself from python/static.

nodes.label: Servo Control App Manifest
nodes.rationale: Declares the sketch path, the python path and main.py as the board entrypoint.

nodes.label: Failures Never Distinguishable From Data
nodes.rationale: Root cause shared by a chain of four defects: a failed read produced an all-zero snapshot that was indistinguishable from a genuine reading of position 0, so downstream code stored it as truth.

nodes.label: TelemetrySnapshot.valid
nodes.rationale: The sketch always sent a valid flag as field 0, but Python parsed and discarded it. Adding the field lets an unanswered read stop masquerading as position zero.

nodes.label: InvalidReadingError
nodes.rationale: Calibration must refuse a reading the servo never gave; previously it stored the zero that made half the travel unreachable. Surfaces as HTTP 409 reason=invalid_reading.

nodes.label: OutOfTravelError
nodes.rationale: Unreachable targets are refused rather than silently clamped, as HTTP 422 reason=out_of_travel naming the range that IS reachable.

nodes.label: Centre-Of-Travel Default Baseline
nodes.rationale: With no datum captured the baseline used to be count 0, putting the entire negative half out of reach before the operator touched anything. Now counts_per_turn / 2.

nodes.label: Off-Centre Datum Warning
nodes.rationale: If the captured datum leaves part of the configured window unreachable, log it with numbers rather than let a servo that stops early reveal it.

nodes.label: Bridge Serialisation RLock
nodes.rationale: An RLock plus a 0.25s read cache: the sampler thread and every HTTP request called Bridge.call concurrently, and interleaved message ids produced 'Response for unknown msgid' and 10s timeouts.

nodes.label: Silent Servo Clamping
nodes.rationale: The servo is configured min angle limit 0, max 4095 and clamps silently: it stops at 0 and still acknowledges the command, so nothing upstream sees a failure.

nodes.label: Datum At Zero Strands The Negative Half
nodes.rationale: With the baseline at count 0, -90 deg maps to count -1502, which the servo cannot reach. Reproduced by the native test range_a_datum_at_zero_strands_the_negative_half.
nodes.norm_label: datum at zero strands the negative half

nodes.label: Coverage Is Not Correctness
nodes.rationale: 100% line coverage did not stop any of the six defects: it means every line ran, not that every assumption was questioned.

nodes.label: Relay And Controller Have No Automated Coverage
nodes.rationale: Every bug in this project lived in the relay and controller: available() vs accept(), accept-before-detect ordering, the missing yield, the missing lock. Native tests cover pure maths only.
nodes.norm_label: relay and controller have no automated coverage

nodes.label: Native Tests Cover Pure Maths Only
nodes.rationale: 164 host checks cover sign-magnitude decoding, angle conversion and status bits. None of the six defects were maths, so the suite could not have caught them.
nodes.norm_label: native tests cover pure maths only

nodes.label: Working Relay Reference Implementations
nodes.rationale: 4_relay_sketch_ino.txt and 5_relay_main_py.txt are the working relay. Consulted when a rewrite went wrong; that is exactly how the accept() bug was found.

nodes.label: servo_truth.md Register Reference
nodes.rationale: ST3215 register map, units, and every value tagged VERIFIED or BENCH.

nodes.label: Network Options Tradeoff Study
nodes.rationale: Why the Ethernet-shield relay was chosen. Read before anyone proposes changing the network architecture.

nodes.label: Servo Diagnostic App
nodes.rationale: Re-run it whenever hardware behaviour is in doubt; it produced most of the verified numbers.

nodes.label: Locked Decisions
nodes.rationale: A table of settled choices that must not be re-litigated: travel window, no framework, LCARS theme, typed inputs, timestamp naming and CSV bridge payloads.

nodes.label: Known Gaps
nodes.rationale: Relay and controller have no automated coverage, OnTarget has never been uploaded, and 100% coverage prevented none of the six defects.

nodes.label: Attach PROJECT_STATE At Chat Start
nodes.rationale: Replaces carrying the old conversation: the reasoning that matters was written down rather than left in a transcript.

nodes.label: GitHub Issue Tracker
nodes.rationale: Issues live in GitHub Issues for Picard1203/servo_mvp, driven through the gh CLI, with PRs deliberately not treated as a request surface.

nodes.label: IPAddress Cast Patch For Ethernet 2.0.2
nodes.rationale: The Zephyr core ships its own arduino::IPAddress, making IPAddress(0ul) ambiguous against three constructors. Fix is an explicit cast at each call site in EthernetClient.cpp, in both branches of the ESP8266/ESP32 #if.

nodes.label: Use SMS_STS, Never SCSCL
nodes.rationale: SCSCL is the SC series and its register map differs: mode is at address 19 there, 33 here.

nodes.label: Vendored Arduino Libraries
nodes.rationale: Patched Ethernet and SCServo live in libraries/ and are referenced by sketch.yaml so nothing is fetched at build time. The folder name must match the sketch.yaml entry.

nodes.label: Dev And Test Dependencies
nodes.rationale: Adds pytest, pytest-cov and httpx on top of the runtime set.

nodes.label: Runtime Dependencies
nodes.rationale: fastapi, uvicorn and pydantic-settings only; a deliberately small surface for an air-gapped wheelhouse.

nodes.label: Six-Fault Status Grid
nodes.rationale: Overload, Current, Heat, Voltage, Sensor and Angle tiles mirroring the six decoded status flags.

nodes.label: Angle And Speed Move Controls
nodes.rationale: Typed text inputs with 0.06 degree nudge steps for angle and 5 deg/s steps for speed, matching the one-count output resolution.

nodes.label: Calibrate Control
nodes.rationale: Confirm-dialog guarded control that captures the datum.

nodes.label: Saved Positions
nodes.rationale: Named position list with save, use and remove actions.

nodes.label: Export 24h CSV
nodes.rationale: Exports the last 24 hours of telemetry; the CSV first column is timestamp.

nodes.label: Duplicate app.js Script Tag
nodes.rationale: index.html includes <script src="/app.js"> twice at the end of body, so the GUI script is fetched and evaluated twice.

nodes.label: Offline Wheelhouse
nodes.rationale: Empty on purpose; fill it on a connected machine and then the whole project folder is the air-gap bundle. Install with pip --no-index --find-links=wheelhouse.

nodes.label: ARM64 Platform Wheels Required
nodes.rationale: The board is ARM64, so wheels must be downloaded with --platform manylinux2014_aarch64. Wheels built for the laptop's architecture will not install there.

nodes.label: src/ Avoids .ino Preprocessing
nodes.rationale: Arduino compiles src/ recursively and does no preprocessing on .cpp/.h files. Only .ino files get concatenated and have prototypes generated, so logic in src/ is ordinary reviewable C++.

nodes.label: AngleConverter
nodes.rationale: Converts counts to and from output degrees including direction sign.

nodes.label: SignMagnitude
nodes.rationale: STS wire-format decode; the source of the 'reads 32700' bug.

nodes.label: ServoFaults
nodes.rationale: Decodes status register 0x41 into six named flags.

nodes.label: ServoBus
nodes.rationale: The only place that touches the serial bus: retries and the EEPROM unlock ritual.

nodes.label: ServoController
nodes.rationale: The operations the backend asks for.

nodes.label: SpiRemap
nodes.rationale: Routes SPI2 to the ICSP header so the Ethernet shield is visible.

nodes.label: NetworkRelay
nodes.rationale: Shield to Linux byte pump with a callback seam and no Bridge dependency.

nodes.label: BridgeApi
nodes.rationale: The contract with Python; the only file that knows payload formats.

nodes.label: App Composition Root
nodes.rationale: Builds the object graph once and drives it; sketch.ino is four lines that hand off to App.

nodes.label: Apply SpiRemap Twice
nodes.rationale: Ethernet.init() re-initialises the SPI pins and undoes the first remap, so it must be applied again afterwards or the W5500 reports 'no hardware'.

nodes.label: Drain With while, Never if
nodes.rationale: The UART RX ring is 64 bytes and socket buffers are small; one byte per loop() is not fast enough.

nodes.label: TinyTest.h Harness
nodes.rationale: About 60 lines and deliberately not AUnit or GoogleTest: every dependency is a liability on an air-gapped machine.

nodes.label: Header-Only Arduino-Free Classes
nodes.rationale: AngleConverter, SignMagnitude and ServoFaults are header-only and Arduino-free on purpose, which is what makes them compilable with plain g++ on a development machine.

nodes.label: Host-Native Test Tier
nodes.rationale: No board, no libraries, milliseconds. Covers sign-magnitude decoding, angle round-trips within one count, the travel window fitting one servo turn, direction mirroring, speed conversion and every status bit.

nodes.label: On-Target Test Tier
nodes.rationale: Covers only what a host cannot: that the servo answers, that configuration writes stick, that a commanded move lands and that stop holds. Not compiled into the main sketch because recursive compilation is limited to src/.

nodes.label: CSV Bridge Payload Contract
nodes.rationale: Plain comma-separated payloads are readable in a log and neither side can drift from a field order the other assumes. Snapshot fields: valid,counts,moving,temp_c,volt_v,curr_a,torque_kgcm,load,status_bits.

nodes.label: .h Files Are Not Auto-Included
nodes.rationale: In a sketch, .h files are not auto-included, which is why every file declares its own includes.

nodes.label: Zephyr UNO Q Board Profile
nodes.rationale: fqbn arduino:zephyr:unoq with the arduino:zephyr platform, pinning SCServo, Ethernet 2.0.2 and Arduino_RouterBridge.

nodes.label: Arduino_RouterBridge
nodes.rationale: Required on the UNO Q for the Linux to MCU Bridge.

nodes.label: Adopt Connections With accept(), Never available()
nodes.rationale: accept() hands over a connection exactly once, transferring ownership. available() returns whichever client has unread data and returns that same client again on every call, so an accept loop built on it adopts one connection into several slots and splits one HTTP request across several sockets.
nodes.norm_label: adopt connections with accept(), never available()

nodes.label: Detect Disconnects Before Accepting
nodes.rationale: Order inside Poll() matters: disconnect detection, then accept, then pump. If accept runs first a just-dropped slot can be handed to a new connection before net_close is sent, and the Linux side feeds new bytes into the old socket.

nodes.label: Edge-Triggered was_up Disconnect Tracking
nodes.rationale: Act on the was-connected to not-connected transition. Testing !connected() every pass emits net_close continuously for slots that are merely idle.

nodes.label: loop() Must Yield
nodes.rationale: Poll() returns immediately when idle so loop() spins at full speed, starving the Bridge RPC thread until servo_read misses its 10s deadline. A delay(1) at the end of Tick() costs nothing against the latency budget.

nodes.label: One Bulk Read Per Slot Per Pass
nodes.rationale: Use client.read(buffer, sizeof(buffer)), not a byte-at-a-time loop, and never block or delay() inside the pump because the same loop() also drives the servo bus.
nodes.norm_label: one bulk read per slot per pass

nodes.label: kRelayChunkBytes Must Match relay_chunk_bytes
nodes.rationale: One number in two places, bytes per Bridge message. Halving it doubles the number of Bridge round trips for identical payload; 256 is the value the working relay used.

nodes.label: Bridge Net Contract
nodes.rationale: MCU to Linux: net_open(slot, client_ip), net_rx(slot, data), net_close(slot). Linux to MCU: net_tx(slot, data), net_shutdown(slot).

nodes.label: provide_safe Registration
nodes.rationale: net_tx and net_shutdown are called from the Bridge thread while loop() may be inside the relay, so they must be registered with provide_safe. Payloads are MsgPack bin_t and must not be packed into a String.

nodes.label: Serial Works; Monitor Is Optional
nodes.rationale: The sketch prints through Serial and that is proven. Monitor (the Bridge console facade) only adds reach to App Lab over WiFi; there is no correctness reason to switch.

nodes.label: Rewriting Instead Of Porting Reintroduced Solved Bugs
nodes.rationale: The relay was once rewritten from scratch instead of ported, and the rewrite reintroduced problems the original had already solved. The reference is the Stage-2 relay sketch.
nodes.norm_label: rewriting instead of porting reintroduced solved bugs

nodes.label: Count (glossary)
nodes.rationale: The servo encoder's unit of absolute position; 4096 per servo turn. Avoid: tick, step, encoder unit.

nodes.label: Output Degree (glossary)
nodes.rationale: An angle measured at the mechanism after the 44:30 belt reduction; one count is 0.06 output degrees. Unqualified 'degrees' always means output degrees. Avoid: servo degree, which is the pre-belt angle and a different quantity.

nodes.label: Datum (glossary)
nodes.rationale: The calibration reference captured from a real servo reading, against which output angles are measured. Must sit mid-travel; a datum at count 0 strands the negative half. Avoid: zero point, home, origin, offset.

nodes.label: Zero Reference (glossary)
nodes.rationale: A saved, named baseline position an operator can recall. The datum is one distinguished zero reference, not a separate kind of thing. Avoid: preset, bookmark, waypoint.

nodes.label: Travel Window (glossary)
nodes.rationale: The reachable output-angle range, plus/minus 90 degrees by default. A target outside it is refused as out_of_travel, never clamped. 180 degrees of output is 3004 counts, inside one servo turn. Avoid: range, limits, bounds.

nodes.label: Snapshot (glossary)
nodes.rationale: One instantaneous sensory readout from the servo, carrying its own valid flag. An invalid snapshot is a failed read, not a reading of zero. Avoid: reading, poll, sample.

nodes.label: Sample (glossary)
nodes.rationale: One persisted telemetry row, written by the sampler at the configured interval and subject to retention. Avoid: snapshot, record, datapoint.

nodes.label: Fault (glossary)
nodes.rationale: One of six conditions decoded from status register 0x41: overload, overcurrent, overheat, voltage, sensor, angle. Avoid: error; alarm is the UI's word for a surfaced fault.

nodes.label: timestamp (glossary)
nodes.rationale: The time field on every entity, schema, DB column, CSV column and query param, spelled out everywhere. Avoid: ts, time, when.

nodes.label: Bridge (glossary)
nodes.rationale: The RPC channel between the Linux side and the MCU. Calls are serialised; payloads are CSV strings with typed arguments. Avoid: link, IPC, channel.

nodes.label: Relay (glossary)
nodes.rationale: The MCU-side byte pump that mirrors Ethernet-shield connections to the Linux side. Owns no HTTP knowledge; it moves bytes. Avoid: proxy, tunnel, forwarder.

nodes.label: Slot (glossary)
nodes.rationale: One mirrored TCP connection inside the relay, identified by index, adopted exactly once via accept(). Avoid: socket, connection id, channel.

nodes.label: Lock (glossary)
nodes.rationale: The digital interlock that refuses movement while engaged. Avoid: e-stop, freeze, hold, safety.

nodes.label: Backend (glossary)
nodes.rationale: Which ServoRepository implementation is live, simulated or hardware, selected by use_hardware_servo. Avoid: mode, driver, mock, fake.

nodes.label: Ubiquitous Language Glossary
nodes.rationale: CONTEXT.md carries a Language section defining the project's domain terms with explicit Avoid lists, so issue titles, test names and proposals use one vocabulary. Maintained by the domain-modeling skill.

nodes.label: Air-Gapped Deployment
nodes.rationale: Final deployment is air-gapped; the dev board has WiFi, production ones will not. Develop as if already air-gapped so shipping is 'zip the folder'. Drives the no-framework, no-bricks, vendored-libraries and wheelhouse decisions.

nodes.label: Plain HTML/CSS/JS, No Framework
nodes.rationale: Air-gap: there is no build pipeline to vendor.

nodes.label: LCARS Light Theme With ISA-101 Safety Colours
nodes.rationale: Chosen after many iterations.
nodes.norm_label: lcars light theme with isa-101 safety colours

nodes.label: Typed Inputs, Not Sliders
nodes.rationale: Operators need exact angles.

nodes.label: 0.06 Degrees Per Count
nodes.rationale: 4096 counts per servo turn through a 44:30 belt gives (360/4096)x(30/44) = 0.0599 degrees at the output.

nodes.label: Zero Deadband
nodes.rationale: Measured landing error: 0 gives 0.06 deg, 1 gives 0.10, 8 gives 0.52, 32 gives 1.98.

nodes.label: Speed Saturates Near 1100 Counts/s
nodes.rationale: About 66 deg/s at the output whatever is commanded; acceleration has no measurable effect above about 50.

nodes.label: Serial1 At 1 Mbps
nodes.rationale: Bench-verified reliable: 200 of 200 reads at 220 microseconds.

nodes.label: Read The Working Reference Before Rewriting
nodes.rationale: Several bugs came from re-deriving solved behaviour instead of porting it.
nodes.norm_label: read the working reference before rewriting

nodes.label: Agent Skills Configuration
nodes.rationale: Points agent skills at the issue tracker and domain doc conventions for this repo.

nodes.label: Graph-First Codebase Navigation
nodes.rationale: Query the graphify knowledge graph before grepping or reading source, because a scoped subgraph costs a fraction of the tokens that browsing python/app or sketch/src does. Grep stays correct for editing specific lines.

nodes.label: Graphify Extraction Gaps
nodes.rationale: Graphify has no .ino or .css mapping, so sketch.ino, OnTarget.ino and style.css are skipped unless routed to the C++ grammar manually.

nodes.label: Single-Context Domain Layout
nodes.rationale: One CONTEXT.md at the repo root plus docs/adr/, rather than a CONTEXT-MAP.md pointing at per-package contexts.

nodes.label: Use The Glossary's Vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Name domain concepts using CONTEXT.md's Language section and avoid the listed synonyms. A concept missing from the glossary is a signal: either invented language, or a real gap for domain-modeling.

nodes.label: Domain Skill Chain
nodes.rationale: grill-with-docs runs a grilling session that maintains docs as it goes, delegating to grilling (stress-tests a plan in rounds) and domain-modeling (maintains the glossary and writes ADRs).
